cases.sentence: Полковой ___ Демин занимал большой помещичий дом.
cases.explain: Командир is the subject of занимал (occupied), so it stands in the nominative case.
After the numeral три (three), the noun takes the genitive singular form.

cases.sentence: Кучка солдат... подошли вместе с Вронским к ___.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Он подошел к Вронскому, пожимая ему ___.
cases.explain: Руку is the direct object of пожимая (shaking), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: За полковым командиром с ___ в руке, улыбаясь, вышел и Серпуховской.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: А мне сказал Яшвин, что ты в своем мрачном ___.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) governs the prepositional case here, describing a state of mind.

cases.sentence: Он подошел к ___, пожимая ему руку и отводя его в сторону.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case, here with the surname Vronsky.

cases.sentence: И он торопливо достал из ___ три 100-рублевые бумажки и покраснел.
cases.explain: The preposition из (out of) governs the genitive case.

reading.ru: «Твоя стирка нынче долго продолжалась», — сказал Петрицкий.
reading.question: What does Petritsky say took a long time today?
reading.explain: Petritsky remarks that Vronsky's 'laundry' — his metaphor for sorting out his affairs — went on a long time today.

reading.ru: «Кончилось», — отвечал Воронский, улыбаясь одними глазами и покручивая кончики усов так осторожно, как будто после того порядка, в который приведены его дела, всякое слишком смелое и быстрое движение может его разрушить.
reading.question: How does Vronsky answer and behave when asked if he is finished?
options: He says 'Finished,' smiling only with his eyes and carefully twirling his mustache, as if any bold movement could undo the order he'd achieved
He angrily denies anything is wrong
reading.correct: He says 'Finished,' smiling only with his eyes and carefully twirling his mustache, as if any bold movement could undo the order he'd achieved
reading.explain: He answers 'Finished,' smiling only with his eyes and twirling his mustache carefully, as if a sudden movement might upset the order he had just achieved.

reading.ru: «Я от Грицки», — так они звали полкового командира.
reading.question: What nickname did the officers use for the regimental commander?
reading.explain: The text explains that 'Gritska' is what they called the regimental commander.

reading.ru: Вронский, не отвечая, глядел на товарища, думая о другом.
reading.question: What was Vronsky doing while Petritsky spoke to him?
options: Looking at his comrade without answering, thinking of something else
reading.correct: Looking at his comrade without answering, thinking of something else
reading.explain: Vronsky, without replying, gazed at his comrade while thinking of something else.

reading.ru: Серпуховской приехал?
reading.question: What news does someone ask about, hearing the sound of music and festivities?
options: Whether Anna had come to visit
reading.explain: Hearing the festive music, someone asks whether Serpukhovskoy had arrived.

reading.ru: Улыбка его глаз заблестела еще ярче.
reading.question: How did Vronsky's expression change on learning Serpukhovskoy had arrived?
options: The smile in his eyes grew even brighter
reading.correct: The smile in his eyes grew even brighter
reading.explain: On hearing the news, the smile in Vronsky's eyes shone even brighter.

reading.ru: Полковой командир Демин занимал большой помещичий дом.
reading.question: What kind of building did the regimental commander Dyomin occupy?
reading.explain: The regimental commander Dyomin occupied a large manor house.

reading.ru: Все общество было на просторном нижнем балконе.
reading.question: Where was the whole company gathered?
reading.explain: The whole company was gathered on the spacious lower balcony.

reading.ru: За здоровье нашего бывшего товарища и храброго генерала князя Серпуховского! Ура!
reading.question: What toast did the regimental commander propose?
options: To the health of their former comrade, the brave general Prince Serpukhovskoy
To the health of the Tsar
reading.correct: To the health of their former comrade, the brave general Prince Serpukhovskoy
reading.explain: The commander raised a glass and proposed a toast to their former comrade, the brave general Prince Serpukhovskoy.

reading.ru: Вронский три года не видал Серпуховского.
reading.question: How long had it been since Vronsky had last seen Serpukhovskoy?
reading.explain: The text states Vronsky had not seen Serpukhovskoy for three years.

reading.ru: Улыбка радости осветила лицо Серпуховского.
reading.question: How did Serpukhovskoy react on catching sight of Vronsky?
options: A smile of joy lit up his face
reading.correct: A smile of joy lit up his face
reading.explain: A smile of joy lit up Serpukhovskoy's face when he saw Vronsky.

reading.ru: И он торопливо достал из бумажника три 100-рублевые бумажки и покраснел.
reading.question: What did Serpukhovskoy do with money from his wallet, blushing as he did it?
options: He hurriedly took out three 100-ruble notes to be distributed among the soldiers
He paid off a gambling debt
reading.correct: He hurriedly took out three 100-ruble notes to be distributed among the soldiers
reading.explain: Serpukhovskoy hurriedly pulled three 100-ruble notes from his wallet, blushing, to be handed out among the men.

reading.ru: Кутеж у полкового командира продолжался долго.
reading.question: How long did the revelry at the regimental commander's continue?
reading.explain: The carousing at the regimental commander's house went on for a long time.

reading.ru: Пили очень много.
reading.question: How much did the officers drink at the party?
reading.explain: The text says simply that they drank a great deal.

reading.ru: Серпуховской вошел в дом, в уборную, чтобы мыть руки, и нашел там Вронского.
reading.question: Where did Serpukhovskoy find Vronsky washing up?
options: In the washroom of the house
reading.correct: In the washroom of the house
reading.explain: Serpukhovskoy went into the house, into the washroom to wash his hands, and found Vronsky there.

reading.ru: – Она дружна с Варей, и это единственные женщины петербургские, с которыми мне приятно видеться, – улыбаясь, ответил Вронский.
reading.question: With whom does Vronsky say Anna is friendly, making them the only Petersburg women he enjoys?
reading.explain: Vronsky says Anna is close with Varya, making them the only two Petersburg women whose company he enjoys.

reading.ru: Серпуховской улыбнулся.
reading.question: How did Serpukhovskoy react to Vronsky's remark about the 'only' women he liked?
reading.explain: Serpukhovskoy simply smiled in response.

reading.ru: Я тоже думал, а вот живу и нахожу, что не стоит жить только для этого.
reading.question: What does Vronsky say about living solely for ambition and success?
options: That he too once thought that way, but now finds it isn't worth living for that alone
That he never thought about it at all
That it is the only thing worth living for
That he plans to retire from the army immediately
reading.correct: That he too once thought that way, but now finds it isn't worth living for that alone
reading.explain: Vronsky says he used to think the same, but living it he finds it is not worth living only for that.

reading.ru: России нужны люди.
reading.question: According to Serpukhovskoy, who needs strong, independent people like him and Vronsky?
reading.explain: Serpukhovskoy insists that Russia needs such people.

reading.ru: Вронский слушал внимательно.
reading.question: How does Vronsky listen to Serpukhovskoy's arguments about power and society?
reading.explain: The text says Vronsky listened attentively.

reading.ru: – Все-таки мне недостает для этого одной главной вещи, – ответил он, – недостает желания власти.
reading.question: What does Vronsky say he lacks for the ambitious path Serpukhovskoy proposes?
options: The desire for power, which he once had but which has passed
reading.correct: The desire for power, which he once had but which has passed
reading.explain: Vronsky says he lacks one main thing — the desire for power, which he once had but that has now passed.

reading.ru: Я только прошу у тебя carte blanche.
reading.question: What does Serpukhovskoy ask Vronsky to grant him?
reading.explain: Serpukhovskoy explicitly asks Vronsky for carte blanche, meaning freedom of action.

reading.ru: Женщины — это главный камень преткновения в деятельности человека.
reading.question: What does Serpukhovskoy call 'the main stumbling block' in a man's career?
reading.explain: Serpukhovskoy states that women are the chief stumbling block in a man's activity.

reading.ru: Вронский распечатал письмо и вспыхнул.
reading.question: What happened when Vronsky opened the note delivered by the lackey?
reading.explain: Vronsky opened the letter and flushed (turned red).

reading.ru: – После поговорим, я найду тебя в Петербурге.
reading.question: What does Vronsky tell Serpukhovskoy as he hurries off after reading the note?
options: That he will find him in Petersburg
That he never wants to see him again
That he is leaving the country
That he will write to him tomorrow
reading.correct: That he will find him in Petersburg
reading.explain: As he leaves, Vronsky says he will find Serpukhovskoy in Petersburg.

highlight.question: What is the regimental commander doing when Vronsky arrives at the celebration?
sentences: Полковой командир Демин занимал большой помещичий дом.
Все общество было на просторном нижнем балконе.

На дворе первое, что бросилось в глаза Вронскому, были песенники в кителях, стоявшие подле бочонка с водкой, и здоровая веселая фигура полкового командира, окруженного офицерами; выйдя на первую ступень балкона, он, громко перекрикивая музыку, игравшую оффенбаховскую кадриль, что-то приказывал и махал стоявшим в стороне солдатам.
Кучка солдат, вахмистр и несколько унтер-офицеров подошли вместе с Вронским к балкону.
Вернувшись к столу, полковой командир опять вышел с бокалом на крыльцо и провозгласил тост: – «За здоровье нашего бывшего товарища и храброго генерала князя Серпуховского.
highlight.explain: These sentences show the commander loudly giving orders over music and later raising a glass to toast General Serpukhovskoy.

highlight.question: Why doesn't Serpukhovskoy approach Vronsky right away when he arrives?
sentences: Сходя с лестницы, Серпуховской увидал Вронского.
Улыбка радости осветила лицо Серпуховского.
Он кивнул кверху головой, приподнял бокал, приветствуя Вронского и показывая этим жестом, что не может прежде не подойти к вахмистру, который, вытянувшись, уже складывал губы для поцелуя.
highlight.explain: This sentence explains he cannot leave the sergeant major, who is already forming his lips for a kiss of greeting.

highlight.question: What is Serpukhovskoy's assessment of his career prospects?
sentences: – Не думаю, – опять улыбаясь, сказал Серпуховской.
– Не скажу, чтобы не стоило жить без этого, но было бы скучно.

Разумеется, я, может быть, ошибаюсь, но мне кажется, что я имею некоторые способности к той сфере деятельности, которую я избрал, и что в моих руках власть, какая бы она ни была, если будет, то будет лучше, чем в руках многих мне известных, – с сияющим сознанием успеха сказал Серпуховской.
– И потому, чем ближе к этому, тем я больше доволен.
highlight.explain: This sentence shows his confident belief that his talents and power would benefit the position he seeks.

highlight.question: What does Serpukhovskoy suggest will eventually dissatisfy Vronsky?
sentences: – Прекрасно – на время.
Но ты не удовлетворишься этим.
Я твоему брату не говорю.
Это милое дитя, так же как этот наш хозяин.
– прибавил он, прислушиваясь к крику «ура», – и ему весело, а тебя не это удовлетворяет.
highlight.explain: This sentence predicts that the simple life of military service will not ultimately satisfy him.

highlight.question: What impresses Vronsky most about Serpukhovskoy?
sentences: Вронский слушал внимательно, но не столько самое содержание слов занимало его, сколько то отношение к делу Серпуховского, уже думающего бороться с властью и имеющего в этом свои симпатии и антипатии, тогда как для него были по службе только интересы эскадрона.
Вронский понял тоже, как мог быть силен Серпуховской своею несомненною способностью обдумывать, понимать вещи, своим умом и даром слова, так редко встречающимся в той среде, в которой он жил.
И, как ни совестно это было ему, ему было завидно.
highlight.explain: This sentence identifies his rare talent for thinking, understanding things, and his gift of speech as what stands out in their circle.
